Noxun Engine = SketchUp 2026 Ruby plugin for custom furniture; its outputs (cut lists, VEPO CSV, purchase lists, prices) are used for real orders. Report only concrete defects with a failure scenario (input/state -> wrong result). No style, naming or formatting remarks. Look beyond the changed lines: grep callers, other readers/writers of the same key, and tests/docs that describe the behavior.
Loader/bootstrap (noxun_engine.rb, noxun_engine/main.rb). Check: noxun_engine.rb only registers the SketchupExtension (plus minimum-version and update recovery); VERSION identical in both files and equal to every ?v= in ui/*.html; MIN_SKETCHUP_MAJOR check precedes loading; plugin files only via AppLifecycle.require_part with one message and fail-closed init; menu/toolbar/observers registered once (reload safe); dialogs registered in the shared fit/theme hook; no logic, globals or $LOAD_PATH changes.

Report only concrete defects with a failure scenario (input/state -> wrong result). No style, naming or formatting remarks. Look beyond the changed lines: grep callers, other readers/writers of the same key, and tests/docs that describe the behavior.
Production/price outputs (cut list/BOM, VEPO CSV, purchase list, budget, offer, sheet layout, Kontrola semaphore, exports). Check:
- Single computation: budget is the price authority; offer is a view whose total must equal budget to the cent; exporters are thin adapters (no own dimension/material/ABS/price logic); UI never recomputes. Flag any second formula for the same number.
- VEPO contract (SYSTEM/VEPO_KONTRAKT.md): 9 columns in exact order, ';', all fields quoted, CRLF, UTF-8 without BOM, finished dims rounded to integer mm with NO ABS subtraction, edge codes ''/em-dash/'=' derived from L1/L2/W1/W2, rotation swaps length<->width AND both edge columns, thickness 18.0-19.1->18 and 36.0-38.1->36, thickness <=0 excluded and logged, name <= VepoExport::NAME_MAX (20) cut at token boundary without ellipsis and the cut logged, file slug rules, poznamka compares ABS vs board by canonical group_id with legacy decor fallback.
- Blockers must stop every listed output: newer config_schema (newer_configs collected before the manufactured filter), stale drawers/hinges/flaps, missing kit. A new output or path that skips the gate is a bug; a gate that hides parts silently is a bug.
- Edge cases: zero/negative/NaN/nil dimensions, empty project, missing catalog record, UNI, duplak with/without source link, unknown unit code, 0 quantity, rounding (money cents, m2 2 decimals min 0.01, sheets integer), comma/dot input.
- Aggregation/grouping keys (row_key, material+thickness group): adding a field must not split or merge rows unexpectedly; free board names are never abbreviated or paired.
- Read paths tolerate legacy data (missing key per the field's documented contract: 'unknown' vs default 0; role_key fallback) and never write to the model or disk unless that is the action.
- Settings read from supplier/export settings: unreadable or wrong-shape file -> backup or defaults WITH an admission (banner/ORANGE), never silent defaults.
- Golden fixtures/tests updated consistently with any changed number, column or text.

Noxun Engine = SketchUp 2026 Ruby plugin for custom furniture; its outputs (cut lists, VEPO CSV, purchase lists, prices) are used for real orders. Report only concrete defects with a failure scenario (input/state -> wrong result). No style, naming or formatting remarks. Look beyond the changed lines: grep callers, other readers/writers of the same key, and tests/docs that describe the behavior.
Builders, geometry, observers, undo, placement, ghost and toolbar tools. Check:
- One user action = one start_operation(name, true)...commit_operation; abort_operation on ANY exception; no early return/next leaving it open; no nested op opened by a callee. redraw_with_undo never inside an op. Observer reactions = transparent ops under the @rebuilding guard (no self re-trigger).
- Observer barrier: ScaleWatch.flush_pending!/observer_idle? before an op that mutates geometry or reads config a pending tick may change (else the tick lands on an unrelated undo step).
- Units: stored data mm Float; Length only via units.rb at the drawing boundary; a bare number in geometry is inches. Watch double conversion and inch DC values mixed with mm.
- Rebuild replaces entities and persistentIds: refs held across it must be re-resolved (valid?/deleted?); erase only while iterating a to_a copy; supported overrides/modules preserved.
- Identity = cabinet_id + part_key (board: id + board/main); names/persistentId never; IDs recycled, an ID match alone is no proof. Every copy path (panel, Ctrl+C/V dedup, tool) goes through the builder seam: new id, appliance_refs dropped; direct add_instance of the definition is forbidden.
- Forward guard: config_schema newer than the plugin -> refuse rebuild/mutation BEFORE normalize; guard reads RAW config from the entity, never the panel payload; missing marker = legacy, never blocks. Config-only writes keep the config_schema marker.
- New config field whose silent loss in an older plugin changes production -> CONFIG_SCHEMA bump + STANDARD §13 + whitelist/normalize on read and write paths.
- Min/max: tiny/huge cabinets, zero-size zones, many shelves/fronts, corner and narrow types; plan passes BuildPlan.validate!; references only in plan[:references].
- Rotated, mirrored or scaled instances, nested components, entities deleted by the user between steps.
- Tool callbacks rescue and log (else the tool silently dies); tools/notifications kept referenced.

Noxun Engine = SketchUp 2026 Ruby plugin for custom furniture; its outputs (cut lists, VEPO CSV, purchase lists, prices) are used for real orders. Report only concrete defects with a failure scenario (input/state -> wrong result). No style, naming or formatting remarks. Look beyond the changed lines: grep callers, other readers/writers of the same key, and tests/docs that describe the behavior.
Per-PC persistence and catalogs (%APPDATA%\NOXUN\Engine JSON files: materials, ABS rules, hardware rules/catalog/sets/taxonomy, templates, appliances, dim series, settings, updater). Check:
- Writes go through JsonFileStore (tmp -> fsync -> .bak -> rename). A corrupt or wrong-shape primary must never overwrite the last good .bak; the shape predicate is a POSITIONAL third argument (a keyword arg would swallow string-key hashes).
- Read-modify-write runs under the cross-process lock (e.g. materials.lock) and re-reads from disk inside it (reload!), not the 1 s cache - two SketchUp instances/PCs may write the same file; degraded?/write_gate stays inside the lock right before the write.
- A MISSING file with no .bak (fresh install) legitimately bootstraps from seeds/defaults. An EXISTING file that is corrupt, empty ({}/[]/null), wrong-typed or partially valid: read the good backup, otherwise defaults with an admission; never silently overwritten by seeds/defaults; writes disabled while reading from backup.
- Forward gate: file std/schema newer than this plugin -> read-only, no seed top-up, save refused with a clear message. Older files: migration path for every old_std < N, idempotent, does not lose unknown keys or user edits.
- Seed bumps (SEED_VERSION etc.) patch only untouched rows and do not overwrite user-edited records; seed changes to hardware/ABS/prices are production changes - check that defaults, codes and quantities are right.
- Schema steps are immutable constants; new step = new constant and SCHEMA_CURRENT points to the highest; every SCHEMA/STD/SEED/VERSION constant must appear in SYSTEM/STANDARD.md §13 with the same value.
- Lazy schema markers written only when content really uses the new shape.
- Drawer recipes are immutable: RELEASED.json sha256 must match; a changed recipe is a new recipe id/version, never an in-place edit.
- No writes into the plugin folder; paths with spaces/diacritics handled; no swallowed exceptions.
- Identity normalization (Materials.identity_norm) used on both sides of every comparison.

Noxun Engine = SketchUp 2026 Ruby plugin for custom furniture; its outputs (cut lists, VEPO CSV, purchase lists, prices) are used for real orders. Report only concrete defects with a failure scenario (input/state -> wrong result). No style, naming or formatting remarks. Look beyond the changed lines: grep callers, other readers/writers of the same key, and tests/docs that describe the behavior.
Core Ruby (data contract, identity, validation, checks, lifecycle, Demos client). Check:
- Data contract (SYSTEM/STANDARD.md): one attribute dictionary NOXUN per entity (only exception dynamic_attributes/scaletool); complex data as JSON string in config; instance is the authority, definition only a fallback; mm Float everywhere; units.rb is the only mm<->Length conversion.
- Missing keys follow the field's documented contract (STANDARD.md): some mean 'unknown' and must not become 0, others are documented as 0/default and are deliberately not stored (e.g. fridge mount_offset; missing schema marker = 0 = legacy). Flag only a mismatch with that contract. nil/empty string/invalid JSON handled; std read without .to_i coercion ('1', 1.0, 0 are invalid).
- Grep all other readers of a changed key/function/constant (core, ui, js payloads, tests, docs); renamed/removed keys keep a legacy read path for existing .skp files.
- Version constants: any change of CONFIG_SCHEMA, BuildPlan::SCHEMA, PartKeys::SCHEMA, Store::STD or catalog schema needs migration/forward-guard handling and an updated STANDARD.md §13 row; additive optional plan fields do not bump.
- Kontrola: severity (RED blocks exports, ORANGE warns) per contract; findings never vanish when an ID is missing (stable address).
- No silent rescue; rescue only what is handled and log; Tool/timer callbacks wrapped.
- Forbidden: string eval, Marshal.load on foreign data, $LOAD_PATH/ENV changes, monkey patching, globals, writing to the plugin folder, API off the main thread, new Net::HTTP (Sketchup::Http, request kept referenced). Files load only via AppLifecycle.require_part.
- API introduced in SketchUp 2026.1/2026.2 only behind respond_to? (minimum is 2026.0).
- Document identity: memories bound to a model object must be cleared in Engine.on_document_replaced; DocKey rotates on new/open model.
- Concurrency and staleness: state cached across ticks (selection, model, entity refs, catalogs) may be stale after undo/redo, document switch or another window's write.

Noxun Engine = SketchUp 2026 Ruby plugin for custom furniture; its outputs (cut lists, VEPO CSV, purchase lists, prices) are used for real orders. Report only concrete defects with a failure scenario (input/state -> wrong result). No style, naming or formatting remarks. Look beyond the changed lines: grep callers, other readers/writers of the same key, and tests/docs that describe the behavior.
UI Ruby (Inspector panel callbacks ui/panel/*.rb, Studio and satellite HtmlDialogs). Check:
- add_action_callback: no 'return' inside the block (use next); callbacks registered before show; dialog reference kept; unique preferences_key; Ruby->JS only via to_json in execute_script, never string interpolation of user text.
- Every write handler: document guard foreign_document?/DocKey.foreign? (a mismatching guid always refuses; an empty guid refuses too, except handlers that document tolerate_blank_client: true for older cached DOM), then target re-resolution on the server (entity exists, PID+ID+kind match, IDs are recycled), then guards (baseline/type/thickness/newer_config) - HTML disabled or aria-disabled is not protection. Payload values are untrusted: validate type, range, nil, NaN, empty string, huge numbers, unknown enum.
- Writes to the model: one undo operation, abort on error, observer barrier (ScaleWatch.flush_pending!) before reading/writing config; status message on every refusal (no silent no-op).
- Stale UI: generation tokens, base/pin values (:stale_client) and captured guid must be compared before writing; an echo push must not overwrite a form the user is editing.
- Payload contract with JS: grep the JS consumer for every key added/renamed/removed; numbers in mm; codes (units, severity) translated in JS, user-facing notes produced by the server when the contract says so; nil vs missing key semantics preserved.
- set_on_closed also runs on app quit: do not add SketchUp API calls there. Closing/reopening a dialog, two open documents, dialog opened before the model is ready.
- Update barrier: new plugin dialogs must be added to every close list used by the updater.
- Long texts (customer names, material names) and diacritics flow intact through JSON; file dialogs return nil on cancel.
- Messages shown to the user come from one place; changed wording/keys checked against tests and JS that match on them.

Noxun Engine = SketchUp 2026 Ruby plugin for custom furniture; its outputs (cut lists, VEPO CSV, purchase lists, prices) are used for real orders. Report only concrete defects with a failure scenario (input/state -> wrong result). No style, naming or formatting remarks. Look beyond the changed lines: grep callers, other readers/writers of the same key, and tests/docs that describe the behavior.
UI JavaScript (CEF 137 in SketchUp HtmlDialog; no CDN, no modules/bundler; Node tests in tests/js). Check:
- Ruby<->JS contract: every key read here exists in the Ruby payload (grep ui/panel/*.rb, *_dialog.rb, production_core.rb) with the same name, type and unit (mm); missing/null keys handled (legacy payloads, empty lists, first push before init).
- Write calls to sketchup.* carry the document guid via nxDocPayload and the guid captured when the action was scheduled (debounced/deferred actions), plus base/generation values where the server checks staleness.
- Delegated click handlers must not send when the element is aria-disabled; double submit prevention; Escape closes only the topmost overlay; listeners not added twice on re-render.
- XSS/HTML injection: any user or catalog text (names, notes, decor) inserted via innerHTML must be escaped (nx_esc); attribute values quoted.
- Numbers: use the nxf* formatters (decimal comma, never hide precision, money in cents, unit codes translated by nxfUnit); parsing accepts comma and dot; NaN/empty/negative inputs rejected before sending.
- Client must not recompute prices, quantities or statuses the server owns, nor derive texts the server sends (e.g. newer_config_note).
- Re-render must not discard what the user is typing (focus, pending edits) unless intended; stale responses after document switch ignored.
- Theme: JS fallback mirrors Ruby (unknown -> noxun); preview.js colors mirror tokens.
- Long names, many rows, empty states, narrow window widths.
- Each tests/js/test_*.js runs as a separate node process; harnesses (minidom) must still load changed files - check that new globals/functions used here exist in the harness or stub.

Report only concrete defects with a failure scenario (input/state -> wrong result). No style, naming or formatting remarks. UI HTML/CSS (panel.html, studio.html, panel.css). Check:
- Cache-bust: every ?v= in ui/*.html equals VERSION exactly (noxun_engine.rb); any css/js change requires a VERSION bump and all ?v= updated.
- Colors only via var(--nx-*) tokens defined in :root (an undefined token silently drops the property); no new hex literals except theme swatches; semantic families (action green, select teal, danger red, warn amber, ABS, edge, state) not mixed; theme may only switch the selection family.
- Radius 6 px for components, 8 px larger surfaces, 9 px badge; 4/5/7 px forbidden.
- No emoji or unicode glyphs as controls; icon buttons have aria-label and title saying what they do.
- Unavailable action uses aria-disabled with explanation, not HTML disabled; computed outputs are text, not readonly inputs.
- Dropdowns/overlays are position:absolute and must not change vertical layout; vertical space in the panel is scarce.
- Every script referenced exists, load order respects dependencies (win_fit.js in every window), no external URLs/CDN.
- IDs/classes used by JS still exist after markup changes (grep ui/js).

Noxun Engine = SketchUp 2026 Ruby plugin for custom furniture; its outputs (cut lists, VEPO CSV, purchase lists, prices) are used for real orders. Report only concrete defects with a failure scenario (input/state -> wrong result). No style, naming or formatting remarks. Look beyond the changed lines: grep callers, other readers/writers of the same key, and tests/docs that describe the behavior.
Dev/test scripts (Windows PowerShell 5.1, Ruby, Node, Python helpers). Check:
- PowerShell 5.1 compatibility: no &&/||, ?:, ??, ?.; native exe errors: $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' plus $LASTEXITCODE checks; 2>&1 on native commands creates error records.
- Paths contain spaces ('C:\APP DEV\...') and non-ASCII: always quoted, Join-Path, -LiteralPath where wildcards matter. Encoding of written files (UTF-8 without BOM where Ruby/JS reads them; PS 5.1 Set-Content defaults to ANSI).
- Locks and collisions: exclusive deploy.lock and last_run.txt sentinel; lock released in finally on every exit path; stale lock from a crashed previous run detected (PID alive?) without deleting a live one; per-run run_* folders with unique names (time + PID); exit codes documented (2 = another run).
- Never kill SketchUp or other processes blindly; never touch a model other than the copy of _dev/ENGINEtests.skp; never deploy into or test against a customer model; -CloseWhenDone semantics preserved.
- Polling: timeouts, result read only after the end marker, partial/old result files from previous runs not mistaken for the current one (mtime/run id).
- Inputs from previous failed runs (leftover temp files, missing recordings, success markers) handled; cleanup does not delete user data.
- Scripts used by CI or hooks keep the exit code contract (non-zero on failure).
